correctness.rationale: Obtained the complete Gao--Shan arXiv:2609.18237 HTML and inspected its exact Theorem 11, Lemma 9 increment (46), six-regime procedure and Remark 30 cost. Theorem 11's one-sided uniqueness is precisely U_c or U_r on the packet D, with acyclicity or integral slack ensuring the greedy chain's feasibility; those are already supplied by source for its actual packets, so the new data structure changes evaluation cost, not mathematical selection. From (46), selecting x with indices (i,j) decrements future δ at all y with i(y)=j and all y with j(y)=i. Under U_c the first is a uniform lazy offset on group G_j; the second touches at most one candidate because any shared i lies in I∩J. U_r gives the symmetric grouping. Local heaps plus a global heap, comparing (δ,numerical index) to preserve source tie-breaking, perform each select/decrement/delete in O(log |D|); initialization O(|D|), and disjoint-index packets satisfy uniqueness vacuously. Nested selected sets/packets contain at most N2 distinct middle words overall, so total O(N2 log N2). For longest words, a word is admissible iff its length-r prefix is in P and suffix in S. If L≥2r, enumerate P×X^(L−2r)×S; if r<L<2r, overlap β=2r−L and enumerate disjoint products P_a×S_a. Each pair creates exactly one word and every admissible word appears once. Build P_a/S_a in one O(N2) pass using numeric membership in natural-order F1 and a bitset F2, then stop after μ3 outputs, costing O(μ3 L) for explicit symbols. Combined bound and stated storage follow in source's unit-cost word-index model. The attached finite verifier is corroborative only, not proof of all parameter regimes.
